| [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md) | Martínez — information-processing view of representation | A state counts as a representation when it shows adaptations for transmitting information for its own sake, i.e. for efficiently trading off rate, distortion and coder complexity — and that trade-off is what grounds the properties cognitive scientists attribute to representations. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-166.md) | Personal Identity and Ethics (SEP) | Which theory of persistence is true (psychological or biological), and whether identity or only the relations composing it is what matters, jointly settle a family of ethical questions — prudence, responsibility, abortion, advance directives, distributive justice — and the priority between metaphysics and ethics is itself unsettled. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-167.md) | Studying philosophy makes people better thinkers | In HERI longitudinal data on over half a million US undergraduates, philosophy attracts students who are already verbally stronger and more curious and open-minded, yet after adjusting for freshman-year baselines philosophy majors still outperform all other majors on GRE Verbal, LSAT and a Habits of Mind measure. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-168.md) | Hartmann & Trpin — Coherence-based explanatory power | Probabilistic measures of explanatory power survive Lange's entailment problem and Roche & Sober's "Two Likelihood Inequalities" critique if explanatory power is measured as how well the whole set of explanantia coheres with the explanandum versus with its negation — in particular using the CohOG+ coherence measure. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-169](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-169.md) | Seth — Conscious AI and biological naturalism | Conscious AI needs both computational functionalism and enough substrate flexibility to run consciousness-relevant computations in silicon, and both are doubtful. Seth argues that positive, non-vitalist reasons from predictive processing, the free energy principle and autopoiesis tie consciousness to being alive, so real AI consciousness is unlikely on current trajectories, while conscious-*seeming* AI is nearly inevitable and ethically pressing. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md) | Takola & Schielzeth — Hutchinson's niche for individuals | A Hutchinsonian niche can be scaled down to single organisms if it is defined as the environmental conditions under which a particular individual has an expected lifetime reproductive success of at least one. Doing so forces a split between realized and potential niches, a choice among time-slice, prospective and trajectory views, and extra intraspecific dimensions. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-171.md) | Algorithmic nudging needs interdisciplinary oversight | Because AI systems can learn nudges that exploit biases nobody has documented, judging algorithmic nudges by predictive success alone repeats Friedman's instrumentalism, and Hausman's "look under the hood" rejoinder supports mandatory oversight by experts in human cognition. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-172.md) | Watson — On the philosophy of unsupervised learning | Clustering, abstraction and generative modelling give data-driven, testable operationalizations of old metaphysical questions (natural kinds, essence vs contingency, modality), but their outputs are not "objective" — they are conditioned on human-chosen data and hyperparameters, so they call for a pragmatic, error-statistical stance. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md) | Griesemer & Shavit — Scaffolding individuality (3Cs) | Evolutionary transitions in individuality can be described without circularity as an idealized developmental sequence of interaction types: coordination in "collections", cooperation in "conexuses", collaboration in "communities". On this view individuality is a special case of collectivity, and new levels of individuality and new inheritance systems evolve in tandem. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-174.md) | Rovelli — The relational interpretation (RQM) | RQM dissolves the measurement problem by treating quantum theory as a theory of sparse facts that are relative to interacting systems, with transition amplitudes yielding probabilities only when their arguments are facts relative to the same system, and decoherence making some facts approximately stable. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md) | Chen — Realism about the Wave Function | A realist about quantum mechanics has three families of options for what the wave function is — a physical object (ontological), something law-like (nomological), or an entity of its own kind (sui generis) — and which ones are available depends on the chosen solution to the measurement problem. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-176.md) | Šekrst — Do LLMs Hallucinate Electric Fata Morganas? | Hallucinations are outputs that diverge from what the source or training data supports, and an LLM's self-reports of emotion or sentience fall under that definition. Šekrst argues that any real machine consciousness might therefore stay epistemically inaccessible, indistinguishable from a sufficiently advanced hallucination. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-177.md) | Turner — Ultrafilters as Propositional Theories | Filters and ultrafilters, and with them Łoś's theorem and compactness, become accessible to philosophers once read as propositional theories: sets of possible-worlds propositions that are consistent and closed under conjunction and implication, and, for an ultrafilter, negation-complete. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md) | De Haro & Butterfield — Philosophy and Physics of Duality | A duality is an isomorphism between models that represent a common core ("bare") theory. Dual models are physically equivalent only when their interpretation maps commute with the duality map, and on the authors' account dualities neither favour structural realism nor create an in-principle underdetermination threat to cautious scientific realism. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-179.md) | Brandom, inferentialism and meaning entitlement | Boghossian's objection to substantive, entitlement-based theories of meaning (drawn from pejoratives like "Boche") works against Dummett but not against Brandom. Brandom's material inferences are non-monotonic and ceteris paribus, so one can grasp a concept while refusing to endorse the inferences it licenses. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md) | Clark & Chalmers — The Extended Mind | When an external resource is coupled with an organism in a two-way interaction and plays the role an internal process would, it is part of the cognitive process. Clark and Chalmers argue that dispositional beliefs themselves (Otto's notebook) can be partly constituted by the environment, provided the resource is reliably available, easily accessed and automatically endorsed. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-181.md) | The Moral Status of Animals (SEP) | No candidate capacity yet proposed (species membership, personhood, rationality) picks out all and only humans as morally considerable, so the live questions are which interests animals have and how their claims weigh, not whether they count. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-182.md) | Arsiwalla et al. — Pregeometry and formal language | The authors propose that Wheeler's "pregeometry" is best modelled as "structureless structure" — the syntactic types and compositional rules of a formal language such as homotopy type theory — adopting a constructivist coherentism in which space and geometry are built from relations rather than a material substrate. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-183.md) | Birch — AI Consciousness: A Centrist Manifesto | Two challenges — users misattributing human-like consciousness to chatbots, and the real but untestable-for-now possibility of profoundly alien AI consciousness — must be met together. Birch argues this means nudging users out of the "persisting interlocutor illusion" without denying that AI could be conscious, while building research programmes, via comparative animal-consciousness science, that could test both computational-functionalist and biological-naturalist claims. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-184.md) | SEP — Units and levels of selection | The "units of selection" debate bundles four separable research questions — interactor, replicator/reproducer, manifestor-of-adaptation and beneficiary — pursued by two multilevel schools (Wrightian evolutionary-change and Fisherian adaptationist/kin-selection) with different models, so many apparent disagreements are answers to different questions. | Skimmed |
